overview: Akila Subramaniam is a tenured Associate Professor as well as Division Director in the Division of Maternal-Fetal Medicine as well as the Director of the OBGYN Research and Diagnostic Laboratory, Vice-Chair of Education, and the Bruce Harris Jr. Endowed Professor in OBGYN. She completed her bachelor degree in Management Science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Shen then went on to complete her medical degree and a master’s in public health at the Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center in New Orleans, Louisiana. She completed her residency as well as a dual fellowship in Maternal-Fetal Medicine and Medical Genetics. Given dual certification in MFM and genetics, Dr. Subramaniam’s clinical interest include fetal ultrasound, prenatal genetic diagnosis, and high-risk obstetrics. Current research interests include outcomes based studies and clinical trials of prenatal and obstetric interventions to decrease the risk of maternal and neonatal morbidity. These have largely focused on puerperal infection, obstetric hemorrhage and thromboprophylaxis, as well as evaluating pathways for preterm birth.
